events.title: Victory Day in Europe (Soviet Union and Russia)
events.description: Following the German Instrument of Surrender signed late on May 8 in Berlin, it was already May 9 in Moscow, and the Soviet Union announced and celebrated the end of the war against Nazi Germany on this date.
events.significance: May 9 became Victory Day, a major commemoration in Russia and several former Soviet states marking the end of World War II in Europe and the immense Soviet losses.

events.title: Schuman Declaration
events.description: French Foreign Minister Robert Schuman proposed placing French and West German coal and steel production under a common High Authority, open to other European countries.
events.significance: The proposal led to the European Coal and Steel Community in 1951 and is considered the starting point of European integration and the European Union; May 9 is celebrated as Europe Day.

events.title: Body of Aldo Moro found
events.description: The body of former Italian Prime Minister Aldo Moro was found in the trunk of a red Renault 4 in Rome, 55 days after he was kidnapped by the Red Brigades.
events.significance: The assassination was a defining moment of Italy's 'Years of Lead,' shaping Italian politics and counterterrorism policy.

events.title: House Judiciary Committee begins Nixon impeachment hearings
events.description: The U.S. House Judiciary Committee opened formal televised hearings on whether to recommend the impeachment of President Richard Nixon over the Watergate scandal.
events.significance: The hearings led to articles of impeachment and Nixon's resignation on August 9, 1974, reinforcing the principle that no one is above the law.

events.title: Italy annexes Ethiopia
events.description: Benito Mussolini proclaimed the annexation of Ethiopia and King Victor Emmanuel III as Emperor following Italy's conquest in the Second Italo-Ethiopian War.
events.significance: The conquest, achieved partly through chemical weapons, exposed the weakness of the League of Nations and foreshadowed the aggression that led to World War II.
